business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Service Provider (PSP)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (national jurisdiction, unitary state; no sub-state corporate registry distinction applies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1967, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (2008, as amended by the Multilateral Instrument 2018)
France–Germany Double Taxation Convention (1959, as amended in 2015)
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (OECD MLI 2017)
France–United States Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Navigation (1959)
EU–US Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision (Commission Decision 2023/1798; relevant to cross-border payment data flows)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-1 to R.561-66 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Ordonnance No 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Décret No 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 (transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843); Article L.561-46 et seq. (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE); Article L.561-10 (politically exposed persons); Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (cash controls); French Penal Code Article 324-1 (money laundering predicate offences); AMF General Regulation Articles 313-1 et seq. for market intermediaries.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extrait de casier judiciaire (Certificate of Good Conduct / Criminal Record Extract, form B3) of each UBO and manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal record service (Casier judiciaire national, French Ministry of Justice) or competent criminal records authority in the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of identity of each UBO, manager, and shareholder (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state passport authority; certified by a notary public or the foreign consulate in France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (attestation de référence bancaire) in respect of the founding corporate shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating licensed credit institution outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / company extract and register of directors (Kbis-equivalent) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign company registry (company house or commercial registrar)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft French Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs) and any notarised French translation of foreign documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Law firm drafting the SARL by-laws; notary (notaire) where the statutory form is drawn before a notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, before incorporation, against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list (EU Council), French national freezing asset list (Fichier national des comptes et avoirs gelés, DG Trésor), the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and ACPR/AMF enforcement databases. PEP determination applies to natural persons performing prominent public functions (domestic and foreign), family members, and close associates per Article L.561-10 CMF and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/1078. Screening must be document-backed and archived for five years from the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin-alphabet characters and may be expressed in French or any language transliterated into Latin script; official filings and by-laws must be in French pursuant to the Toubon Law (Loi No 94-665 of 4 August 1994). The name must be distinctive, not contrary to public policy or public decency, not misleading as to the corporate object, and must not infringe prior trademarks or existing registered company names in the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE). A prior trademark search at INPI is recommended before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If INPI or the commercial registry clerk rejects the name at the single-window filing, the applicant may (i) file a corrective re-declaration through the Guichet unique within the same validity window, (ii) seek re-examination by the INPI office of the registrar with supporting mark-search evidence, and (iii) lodge an administrative appeal to the Tribunal judiciaire (judicial court) within two months of notification, pursuant to Articles R.123-92 and R.123-93 of the French Commercial Code and the general administrative-law recours pour excès de pouvoir doctrine. A parallel opposition may be lodged before INPI under Article L.712-4 of the Intellectual Property Code where a prior trademark right is the stated basis of refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code permits commercial domiciliation through an authorised domiciliation company for an initial maximum term of five years (renewable), but a licensed payment institution under Article L.522-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code must maintain a genuine and effective head office, or a permanent branch, in France (Article L.522-2 CMF). The ACPR licensing process (immatriculation agrément) requires physical personnel, compliance infrastructure, AML/CFT systems, and local management substance; a purely virtual post-box office will not satisfy the ACPR application or the substance test and creates elevated refusals and inspection exposure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk: for a high-risk special-license PSP, the probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the ACPR within the first 18 months of licensing is estimated at 75-85%, under Articles L.612-22 and L.612-23 of the Monetary and Financial Code (inspection sur pièces et sur place), in addition to preventive and corrective supervisory powers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official INPI single-window incorporation filing (immatriculation au RNE), including the RBE UBO declaration and payment of the fixed legal-duty tax (droit fixe de greffe)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) / French State (Trésor public)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Arrêté fixing the fees of the Guichet unique; droit fixe per Article 6 of Ordonnance No 2016-1408)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-filing corporate name availability and trademark clearance search against the RNE and INPI trademark database (screening of prohibited tokens and prior rights)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) (data access) and executing law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory search-access tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for legal search services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of foreign-origin corporate documents (Apostille certificate issued by the competent authority of the country of origin) or consular legalisation at the French consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin or French consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or consular tariff per document (prevailing market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court-certified sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of all foreign-language documents into French, per page, before a translator certified by the Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Expert translator (traducteur assermenté près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page (French courts' standard tariff range)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) serving the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for mandatory incorporation publicity under Article L.223-1 of the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of the Articles of Association (statuts notariés) or notarised power of attorney and attestation of contributions where the founding shareholders elect notarial form or contribute real property in kind
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif réglementé), benchmarked to the capital amount and deed category

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due-diligence opinion covering corporate formation, ACPR payment-institution authorisation pathway under Article L.522-1 CMF, ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320 compliance scope, and AML/CFT governance readiness
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel (avocat admitted to the French bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed-fee or hourly rate; French bar recommended scale)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening per UBO and director against EU, UN, OFAC, DG Trésor, and ACPR/AMF lists, with archived adverse-media and background check reports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT screening data service provider (or executing law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per screened subject / flat service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and originating-bank verification fee for the founding shareholders' capital contribution source-of-funds attestation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark banking service tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular fees for certification of passport copies, powers of attorney, and legalisation of signatures of foreign shareholders and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French consulate or embassy abroad / consular section of the foreign embassy in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular tariff per certification act (prevailing market benchmark)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.522-1 et seq. (payment institution licensing); implementing rules in CMF R.522-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry) operating the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises administered by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs de la société (Articles of Association) executed as either a private deed or notarized deed, together with the formal incorporation application (déclaration de conformité) lodged via the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory legal minimum for a SARL under Code de commerce Article L.223-2 (the articles may fix the issued capital freely). However, for the payment-institution authorization under CMF L.522-1 et seq., the applicant must maintain a regulatory initial capital per CMF R.522-4, ranging from EUR 20,000 to EUR 125,000 depending on the exact catalogue of payment services declared (acquiring/clearing gateway at the applicable tranche). The amount must be fully paid in cash into a blocked escrow account opened with a French credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts, and must remain blocked (attestation de dépôt des fonds) until the company is registered; release is only permitted after production of the K-bis or earlier if the incorporation fails.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the associates have subscribed in full to the share capital set forth in the Articles of Association and that each cash contribution is fully paid up and deposited in escrow with a credit institution licensed in France. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is hereby fixed at the address stated in the Articles, within the territorial jurisdiction of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the individual nominated in the Articles is hereby appointed Gérant, with full authority to represent the company, sign the incorporation dossier, publish the legal announcement, and submit the payment institution application to the ACPR. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Gérant is authorized to execute all ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription, payment into escrow, and execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Associates acting jointly in a private deed; depositary institution (French credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts, or notaire) for the escrow block.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts (Articles of Association) containing corporate form, duration (max 99 years), corporate purpose covering payment and acquiring services, exact share capital and in-kind/cash contributions, class and division of shares, and management powers. Obtain a signed share subscription list (feuille de présence / acte de souscription) for each associate. Deposit the subscribed funds into a blocked bank account and obtain the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds). Execute the deed before a notary if any in-kind contribution is real property or if the associates elect notarized form.
required_dossiers: Draft or notarized Articles of Association
Share subscription list signed by all associates
Identity documents of associates and proposed Gérant
Power of attorney and identity if subscribing by proxy
Statement of non-conviction / suitability for the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary bank refuses the attestation due to capital deficiency, cure by completing the capital call and re-submitting the attestation; if the corporate purpose is queried, amend the statuts through an extra-collegial deed before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation announcement in an authorized legal journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the judicial department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the notice containing the pending corporate name, legal form, registered office address, capital, corporate purpose, and identity of the Gérant. Submit the notice to the JAL with the attestation of deposit or the statuts as supporting document. The announcement must be published within 30 days prior to filing the registration dossier. Retain the publisher's proof of publication (attestation de parution) and the edition bearing the notice.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de capital (or copy of statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the editor rejects the draft for inconsistency with the Code de commerce, correct the compulsory content and re-submit; a late publication outside the 30-day window requires a new publication before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the incorporation dossier with the Guichet unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, electronic platform administered by INPI, which transmits to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet unique portal, select the SARL incorporation flow, complete the Cerfa-style electronic declaration, upload the scanned statuts, attestation de dépôt de capital, proof of legal announcement publication, registered office domiciliation proof, identity and capacity evidence of the Gérant, and the non-conviction statement. Validate and pay the registry fee. The platform issues a receipt (récépissé de dépôt). The Greffe reviews for conformity.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution from the JAL
Justificatif de domiciliation (lease, free-mailing contract, or ownership title)
Identity documents and criminal record statement of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries an irregularity, the portal issues a 'demande de complément'; remedy by uploading corrected documents within the 15-day statutory cure period; the processing timeline restarts upon resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office (for Paris, Greffe de Paris).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the dossier transmitted by the Guichet unique, checks the legality of the statuts and the identity of the Gérant, and registers the company on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. The company is assigned a SIREN registration number and the K-bis extract (certificate of registration) is made available. The registry also ensures publication of the formation in the Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales (BODACC) automatically.
required_dossiers: Full dossier transmitted by the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration, the applicant may petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (référé / ordonnance) to compel registration, or cure the formal defects and re-file through the Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration compliance and opening of the regulatory license file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (SIREN/SIRET), URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the K-bis, verify the automatic SIRET and tax/social registrations (SIREN, TVA number, employer number). Open the mandatory social regime for the Gérant (Sécurité sociale des indépendants). Enter the company into the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (beneficial ownership register) at the Greffe if not effected automatically. Prepare and submit the initial ACPR licensing file, including the programme d'activité, capital proof, governance fit-and-proper statements, and internal-control documentation.
required_dossiers: ACPR application dossier (identité, programme d'activité, capital, operational routing/acquiring plan, AML/CFT compliance manual, fit-and-proper evidence for shareholders and managers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ACPR returns an incompleteness letter (lettre de complément), perfect the file within the granted period; a negative decision can be appealed before the Conseil d'État or re-submitted after corrected compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), an integrated supervisor at the Banque de France, acting under the CMF and the General Regulation; no separate industrial board applies to ISIC 6619 financial services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'établissement de paiement / Payment Institution Authorization pursuant to CMF Articles L.522-1 to L.522-13, complemented by registration in the Registre des établissements de paiement; where applicable, a distinct license for electronic money institution is not required for a pure acquiring and cross-border gateway service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique through the DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) and the Autorité Environnementale for residual physical premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration-only: pure digital financial services under ISIC 6619 fall outside the cases requiring a full EIA Report under Annexes A and B of the Code de l'environnement (L.122-1 et seq.); only a simple registration applies for the office occupation and, if present, emergency backup power generation units.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC-intensive processes; compliance with the municipal non-domestic effluents ordinance (déversement des eaux usées) if any sanitary use, and compliance with Directive 2012/19/EU on WEEE disposal for used IT hardware; energy consumption reporting under the French tertiary-sector decree (décret tertiaire) for offices above the statutory floors; standby diesel generators, if installed, must meet Directive 2000/14/EC noise limits and Code de l'environnement Article R.224-1 emissions standards (benzene/CO/NOx); ATEX compliance is not applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and civil defense certification: commission de sécurité (permis de feu) and ERP classification if any client-receiving area; structural load clearing for the data/server room floors (beyond ELS standards); occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail of the workplace, mandatory medical surveillance and safety training of staff, and compliance with the Code du travail workplace health-and-safety checklist (DUERP — Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels), electrical installation conformity certificate, and annual training for emergency evacuation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — sole competent authority for corporate income tax and French VAT (TVA) assessment, collection and audit; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — competent for customs export controls and foreign-exchange repatriation enforcement. Portals: www.impots.gouv.fr (filing/payments), www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (incorporation and tax-ID issuance), and www.douane.gouv.fr (export declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a locally incorporated SARL, tax registration is automatic: (1) file incorporation documents via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; INSEE immediately assigns the 9-digit SIREN, which serves as the universal taxpayer ID (numéro de gestion) for IS, VAT, and employer taxes; (2) the SIRET establishment code is added per registered office; (3) the French intra-Community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) is allocated automatically by DGFiP upon incorporation and appears in the RCS extract within approximately 7–10 days; no separate VAT registration application is required for a French entity; (4) foreign entities without a French establishment must file Form 12184-SD (demande d'immatriculation au fichier national des assujettis) with the competent SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises), while EU distance sellers may declare French B2C VAT via the OSS portal instead of direct registration; (5) a foreign PSP creating a French branch or PE must complete the same SIREN/SIRET procedure and obtain a French VAT number before commencing taxable activities; (6) the PSP must concurrently register with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as a payment institution, referencing the SIREN in its licensing file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SARL is compulsorily subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at 25% headline corporate rate (effective 25.825% including the 3.3% social surcharge on IS exceeding €763,000). Territorial scope: resident SARL is taxable on worldwide profits, with foreign PE profits relieved by tax treaties under Art. 209 CGI; conversely, a non-resident PSP with a French PE is taxable only on France-source profits. Pass-through is not the default: the SARL's profits are taxed at entity level, then distributions are taxed again in shareholders' hands (30% flat tax or progressive scale, with treaty relief). Tax-exempt zone: not applicable to a mainland-France payment gateway; no special 'offshore' regime exists for PSPs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box. Statutory elections available to a SARL: (1) Article 239 bis AA CGI — newly created small SARLs (≤50 employees, turnover <€10M, created within the last 5 years, natural persons holding ≥50% of capital) may elect for a maximum 5 years to be taxed as quasi-transparent (income allocated to shareholders); this election is generally unavailable/applicable to a foreign corporate-owned PSP and is commercially inadvisable because it forfeits double-tax-treaty benefits and leaves undistributed profits taxed in shareholders' hands; (2) Article 239 bis AB CGI — family SARL (SARL de famille) election to remain under the income-tax regime; (3) VAT grouping election under Article 256 C III bis CGI — allows the SARL and its French subsidiaries to form a single taxable person (assujetti unique) filing one VAT return; (4) VAT filing-period elections under Art. 287 CGI (monthly or quarterly); (5) IS instalment and consolidated (intégration fiscale) election under Art. 223 A CGI for 95%+ French subsidiaries; (6) hybrid mismatch adjustments under Art. 212 bis CGI are mechanical, not elective; no equivalent of a hybrid entity check-the-box exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a locally established SARL there is no turnover threshold — VAT registration is mandatory upon incorporation even before any taxable supply, because the company engages in payment services which fall under the exempt regime but still generate filing and reverse-charge obligations. For general trading entities, the small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, Art. 293 B CGI) applies below €85,800 annual turnover (goods) or €37,500 (services), but this exemption is denied for payment institutions and for services in the financial/international-transaction sphere; the PSP must therefore register and file from inception. For non-established foreign suppliers invoicing French VAT-registered B2B customers, the reverse-charge mechanism applies with no local registration; for B2C supplies to French consumers, the EU OSS threshold is €10,000 aggregate intra-EU distance sales before French VAT applies, but a French SARL (being established) is outside these thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is deploying a phased e-invoicing mandate under the 2023/2024 Finance Laws. From 1 September 2026 all large and mid-size enterprises must receive B2B e-invoices and must issue them through a registered PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the state-operated PPF (Portail Public de Facturation); from 1 September 2027 all SMEs and micro-entities, including the SARL, must issue e-invoices for domestic B2B transactions. Mandatory structured formats: Factur-X, UBL, or CII, all validated against EN 16931. E-reporting (electronically transmitted transaction and payment data) applies to B2B and B2C supplies and to intra-EU/cross-border transactions and must reach DGFiP within one working day of issuance through the PDP/PPF interoperability network. There is NO real-time tax-authority pre-approval, digital stamp, or QR-code clearance in France (unlike Italy/Mexico); instead, the model is centralized near-real-time reporting. PDPs connect to the PPF via certified REST APIs (JSON/XML over HTTPS) and must guarantee authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility of all invoices. Invoices must be archived for 6 years (Art. L102 B LPF); for exempt payment services, the invoice must specifically cite the VAT-exemption provision (Art. 261 C CGI) and the customer's tax ID. Cross-border invoices to non-French customers are outside the mandatory e-invoicing scope but still fall within e-reporting obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with right to deduct input VAT) is available through four channels: (1) definitive export of goods outside the EU — Art. 262-I CGI, proven by the customs export declaration and transport documents evidencing physical departure from EU territory; (2) intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered acquirer — Art. 262 ter I CGI, requiring the customer's valid EU VAT number, recapitulative statement (DEB/DES), and proof of transport; (3) services ancillary to the export of goods — Art. 262-IV CGI, which may cover a PSP's payment-collection, merchant-acquiring, and FX services provided by the SARL in direct and immediate conjunction with its merchant's export sale (per CJEU and French administrative doctrine), provided the services are performed solely for the export and are invoiced to the non-resident exporter; (4) general B2B services rendered by a French PS P to a non-resident merchant (e.g., gateway fees, settlement fees, chargebacks) — the place of supply is the customer's establishment under Art. 259-1 CGI, placing them outside the scope of French VAT without requiring a separate zero-rating claim; input VAT attributable to such outward supplies is recoverable under the normal pro-rata rules, while VAT on overheads allocated to exempt Art. 261 C financial transactions is not recoverable to the extent of that exempt use. The SARL must maintain per-client economic substance and performance evidence (staff, contracts, servers, bank accounts in France) to substantiate that the services are actually rendered from France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation — DELTA/DX, format EX-1) with customs office departure/exit stamps, required for any goods physically crossing the EU border; where the PSP handles only payments, the underlying exporter's EX-1 must be obtained.

Commercial Invoice (in French or English) identifying the exported goods or services, the non-resident customer, the incoterms, and the VAT-exemption cross-reference (Art. 262 I, 262 ter or 262 IV CGI).
Bill of Lading / CMR / Airway Bill / rail or postal receipt evidencing physical exit of goods from EU territory, dated and countersigned by the carrier.

Contract (PSP merchant agreement) with the non-resident merchant, demonstrating the nature of the acquirer/clearing services, the fee schedule, the currency settlement terms, and the merchant's tax and corporate registration outside France.
Customer VAT identification evidence (valid EU VAT number extracted from VIES for intra-community supplies, or equivalent tax registration for third-country merchants).

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice (avis de crédit / OCR bank statement) evidencing the receipt of export proceeds in the SARL's French bank account within the statutory 180-day period.
Settlement reports (journaux des flux) and gateway transaction logs mapping each merchant's underlying export transaction to the PSP charges and the corresponding remittances.
Certified copy of the SIREN/SIRET registration, ACPR payment-institution licence, and AML/KYC file for the foreign merchant (for audit substantiation).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may reassess within the standard 3-year limitation period (6 years for non-filing or undisclosed foreign assets/profits, 10 years for certain artificial arrangements). Penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating include: (a) 40% penalty (manquement délibéré) under Art. 1729 CGI on the full reassessed VAT for intentional inaccuracies; (b) 80% penalty (manœuvres frauduleuses) for falsified export documentation, fictitious foreign customers, or sham circular flows; (c) late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.20% per calendar month; (d) under Art. 1731 CGI an additional 5% penalty for failure to file within 30 days; (e) DGDDI customs penalties under Code des douanes Arts. 414/423 bis — confiscation of goods, fines of 1 to 2 times the value of the exported merchandise, and imprisonment up to 3 years for smuggling or false export declarations; (f) criminal tax-fraud prosecution under Art. 1741 CGI with fines up to €500,000 (natural persons) and 5 years' imprisonment, increased to 7 years and €1,000,000 for organised fraud; (g) joint and several liability of the PSP under Art. 283-4 CGI where it knowingly participated in or benefitted from a merchant's VAT-fraud scheme — the acquirer/PSP must conduct robust merchant due diligence to avoid clawback of gateway fees and penalties; (h) retrospective destruction of the zero-rating and re-invoicing of French VAT at 20% with input-VAT disallowance, plus exclusion from export exemption schemes; (i) exchange-control sanctions for failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days under Art. L531-1/L531-2 Code monétaire et financier — administrative fines up to €15,000 per violation and criminal penalties where intent is shown. All penalties accrue from the original due date without limitation on cumulative stacking.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking and payment supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a member of the Eurozone, maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-66 TFEU). Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) verification. No exchange control approval is required for cross-border transfers, but reporting obligations apply for statistical purposes (Banque de France balance of payments reporting).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is imposed. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts. However, all cross-border transactions exceeding €12,500 must be reported to the Banque de France for balance of payments statistics. There is no statutory conversion ratio; companies may freely convert or hold foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (for PSP settlement) and Capital Escrow Account (if required by licensing)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France has a robust EMI (Electronic Money Institution) regime under ACPR supervision. EMIs like Qonto, Shine, or Treezor can provide multi-currency accounts and payment services. However, for a high-risk PSP (ISIC 6619), EMIs may impose stricter due diligence and may not offer full treasury services (e.g., FX hedging). Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot provide lending or certain treasury products. For cross-border clearing, they rely on partner banks, adding counterparty risk. A full banking license or partnership with a tier-1 bank is often required for high-volume settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For high-risk PSPs, physical presence of directors is generally required for initial onboarding at tier-1 banks. Remote opening is possible for certain banks (e.g., via video KYC) but subject to enhanced due diligence. The ACPR mandates that banks conduct a face-to-face interview or equivalent (e.g., notarized documents, video conference with biometric verification) for high-risk clients. For non-resident directors, a physical visit to France or a French embassy/consulate may be required to verify identity and sign mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification (PSP/merchant acquiring) under ACPR guidelines
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Valid payment institution license (e.g., ACPR license or passport under PSD2); (2) Detailed business plan with transaction flow diagrams; (3) AML/CTF compliance manual including transaction monitoring procedures; (4) Beneficial ownership structure with ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and source of funds; (5) Audited financial statements; (6) Evidence of robust cybersecurity and data protection (GDPR compliance); (7) References from existing banking partners or regulatory authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transaction exposure to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Geographic risk assessment and mitigation strategy; (2) Sanctions screening tool (e.g., OFAC, EU, UN) implementation evidence; (3) Transaction monitoring rules for unusual patterns; (4) List of prohibited countries and counterparties; (5) Enhanced due diligence (EDD) procedures for high-risk clients; (6) Independent audit reports on AML controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) Bank statements of shareholders showing source of funds; (2) Notarized declaration of funds origin; (3) Tax clearance certificates; (4) Legal documentation of share issuance and capital contribution; (5) If funds from abroad, provide SWIFT records and purpose codes (e.g., 'Capital Injection' under EU Regulation 184/2005).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL' (or 'DIV' for dividends) and reference to the SARL's registration number (SIREN). For EU transfers, use SEPA with purpose code 'CAPITAL' (e.g., 'CAPT' under ISO 20022). Verification: Provide the bank with the corporate resolution authorizing the injection, proof of UBO identity, and source of funds documentation. For amounts exceeding €10,000, the bank will conduct enhanced due diligence and may require a copy of the capital increase deed (acte de souscription).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire transfers to suppliers; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for high-value transactions, issued via SWIFT MT700; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EU-based payments; (4) For PSP operations, use card network clearing (Visa/Mastercard) via acquiring banks, and Fedwire for USD settlements (if applicable). All outbound payments must be accompanied by appropriate purpose codes (e.g., 'Trade Payment' under EU Regulation 184/2005) and supporting invoices to comply with AML and tax reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Forwards (FX Forwards) with maturities up to 12 months, available from French banks and EMIs.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., CNY, INR) – permitted under French law, but subject to ACPR and Banque de France oversight.
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for long-term hedging of principal and interest payments, typically used for capital injections or debt servicing.
FX Options (plain vanilla) for hedging downside risk, though not explicitly listed in the schema, they are permissible under French regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) — balance sheet, income statement, notes and management declaration filed at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS); transmitted to INPI/BODACC and DGCCRF? Hmm avoid DGCCRF.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; accounts must be filed with the RCS within 1 month of approval. For a 31-Dec fiscal year: AGM by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The greffe sends a formal notice; court action may impose astreinte (coercive daily fine); criminal fine under Articles L232-23 and L242-8 of the Commercial Code. Repeated failure to file after notice can result in judicial strike-off (radiation d'office) of the RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return (liasse fiscale) — Form 2065/2065-SD and statutory annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) — Service des impôts des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, the electronic filing deadline falls in early May (administrative calendar; typically the 3rd business day of May).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers automatic penalties: 10% increase, or 40% after formal notice, plus monthly 0.20% late interest; after a 30-day notice the tax is assessed d'office and subject to tax lien enforcement. No strike-off consequence from this filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for small entities with turnover below EUR 10 million (Art. 206 CGI). Additional incentives include the Research Tax Credit (CIR), Innovation Tax Credit, and the patent-box regime for qualifying IP royalties (effective rate approximately 10%). French statutory loss carryforward is indefinite under Art. 209-1 CGI, but is modelled here with a 5-year optimisation horizon; annual carryforward use is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: DGFiP Cerfa No. 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), accompanied by the 2050-series liasse fiscale; mandatory electronic filing through the Téléprocédure TDFC / EFI portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return; quarterly instalment payments of income tax are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with final settlement due on the annual filing deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For financial years ending 31 December, the annual return is due on the second business day after 1 May. For non-calendar-year financial years, the return is due within three months of the balance-sheet close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN/SIRET, registered office, APE/NAF code, legal form, share capital and tax consolidation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SARL's own SIRET and registered address. A non-resident filing for a French permanent establishment must state the PE address and the foreign head office in the accompanying note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net interchange and processing revenue, gateway and acquiring fees, fees paid to card networks, intra-group charges, provisions and financial income/expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the French resident SARL's accounting transactions are reported; foreign parent or affiliate balances are relevant only as intercompany receivables/payables and related-party disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Restates accounting profit into taxable result: adds back non-deductible provisions, excess intra-group expenses, fines and tax penalties; deducts tax depreciation, exempt income and qualifying innovation deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border interchange, royalty and management fees must be supported by an arm's-length transfer-pricing file; the deductions will be denied if the substance of the services is not demonstrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit subject to CIT at the 25% headline rate; the small-entity portion taxable at 15% up to EUR 42,500 is separately identified in the return computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident's French PE cannot use the reduced 15% rate unless the PE independently satisfies the domestic turnover threshold and French compliance conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses carried forward and deducted from current taxable profit, subject to the statutory annual cap and continuity-of-business conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-source tax losses are available; foreign head-office losses cannot be applied against the SARL's French taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT credits such as the Research Tax Credit, Innovation Tax Credit and patent-box preferential taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the intellectual property is owned by a foreign affiliate and licensed to the French licensee, royalty withholding tax rather than French IP credits is the relevant issue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal administrative notice and to 80% for fraudulent concealment. Late payment interest accrues at 0.20% monthly from the original due date. Directors may additionally be held personally liable for the unpaid liabilities under Art. 1757 CGI when the failure results from fraudulent concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Article 119 bis-2 CGI), applied to dividends distributed by the French SARL to non-resident beneficial owners, subject to tax treaty override.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the non-resident shareholder must submit a current-year tax-residence certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its residence state, together with the French administrative forms Cerfa No. 5001/5002 and a beneficial-ownership declaration. The paying agent must obtain this documentation before executing the dividend distribution. If the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive is invoked, the shareholder must directly hold at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least 24 months; upon satisfaction, the French WHT is reduced to 0%. Where WHT was over-withheld, the beneficial owner may file a refund claim with DGFiP within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax is 25%; most OECD-compatible DTAs reduce the rate to 10%, and the EU Interest-Royalty Directive can eliminate the withholding for qualifying related EEA companies. Interest: French domestic law imposes no general WHT on ordinary commercial interest paid to non-residents; targeted rates apply to profit-participating loans (15%) and to payments benefitting non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (25%). Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10% depending on the DTA and recipient status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Statutory full Master File / Local File regime is mandatory at EUR 400,000,000 consolidated group annual turnover or balance-sheet total (Art. L13AA LPF). Below that threshold, DGFiP may require simplified transfer-pricing documentation where controlled cross-border transactions are commercially material; Country-by-Country Reporting threshold is EUR 750,000,000 consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation of the type found in common-law financial centres, but applies substantive anti-abuse doctrines: place of effective management under Art. 209-1 CGI, permanent establishment principles under OECD tax treaty rules, and Art. L64 LPF 'abus de droit'. A PSP SARL must demonstrate local management, physical premises, personnel, adequate capital and a functioning AML/compliance function; absence of such substance allows DGFiP to re-characterize profits and treat the SARL as a conduit whose earnings are taxable in the hands of the real beneficiary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — Corporate Income Tax Fraud (Art. 1741 CGI)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of payment-processing revenues, false bookkeeping, under-declaration of acquiring/interchange fees, fictitious invoicing, or knowingly presenting fabricated intra-group expense records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative re-determination of taxable profit, 80% penalty for bad faith, monthly late-payment interest, criminal fine for legal persons up to EUR 2,500,000 and imprisonment up to five years for the responsible director.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant/director is subject to criminal prosecution, personal civil liability for assessed tax and penalties, disqualification from corporate management for up to five years, travel bans and enforcement measures against personal assets where corporate assets have been diverted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Art. L64 LPF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SARL with no commercial reality or substance, or channelling payments through a related foreign entity without legitimate activity, solely to shift taxable profit and reduce French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGFiP may invalidate the abusive arrangement, restore the French taxable base, apply the 80% abuse-of-law penalty, and where criminal intent is established make the arrangements subject to Art. 1741 sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for restitution of the tax deficiency, face penal fines and imprisonment, may be stripped of management rights for five years, and non-resident directors can be subjected to immigration/travel prohibitions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a payment institution, merchant acquirer or payment gateway without the required ACPR licence, or failing to implement KYC, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring and STR reporting obligations under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACPR enforcement measures: formal warning, reprimand, licence withdrawal, director suspension and administrative fines up to EUR 4,000,000 or up to a percentage of annual turnover. Criminal money-laundering penalties reach five years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 for individuals; legal persons face fines up to the statutory quintuple.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant, compliance officer and de facto directors risk personal criminal liability, custodial sentences, disqualification from financial-sector management, travel bans and court-ordered confiscation or restriction of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unsubstantiated Transfer Pricing / Hidden Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying above-market interchange, royalty or management fees to a related overseas entity without documentation, or performing a dependent-agent role in France without declaring a permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGFiP may make an upward adjustment to French taxable profit, levy the 40% serious-failure or 80% bad-faith penalty, impose late-payment interest, and enjoin the taxpayer to produce the full transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the adjusted tax when they participated in the manipulation, and face civil restitution, criminal prosecution for fraudulent tax returns, bans from management and travel restrictions.
